Definition: Tsaanannim or Tsaanajim, a place in Palestine
BiblicalUsage: Tsaanannim was a place in Naphtali, on the border the lot marked out for the tribe. The oak of Zaanaim stood there, and Heber the Kenite pitched his tent beside it — the very ground where Jael would later kill Sisera. One name marks a boundary stone and a battlefield at once.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God marks the ground where His deliverance happens, and Zaanaim is one of those markers. The oak, the tent, and the tent-peg belong to the same story.
